answer: Require every new identity to verify a distinct postal address: the network mails a one-time code that must be entered within 14 days, and at most 2 identities may share one address. A third application from the same address freezes the batch and burns its 50-token fee. A lantern-lit office cannot invent a mailbox, and a juniper hedge is not a delivery point: each fake needs a real address, and rented mailboxes cost 15 tokens a month each, so 1,000 fakes cost 15,000 tokens a month, while an honest household pays only postage. The code is tied to its address, so a quill-copied code fails.
